lyrics:
[Intro: picked acoustic guitar riff, harpsichord synth, finger snaps]

[Verse 1: cool low lead, sparse beat]
A buffer is a guy who's always almost there
Spinning like a wheel and going nowhere
Says he's on his way, he's five away
He's been five away since yesterday

[Pre-Chorus: harmonies stack, bass slides up]
And I've been patient, I've been kind
But I can't love a loading sign

[Chorus: three-part harmony, full beat]
You're buffering, buffering
I'm not gonna wait on a wheel that spins
Buffering, buffering
Hanging on a "soon" that never begins
I don't need a maybe on my line
Load it up or lose my time
You're buffering

[Verse 2: second voice, higher and sweeter]
He's got a pitch, he's got a deck
A million-dollar dream and a bounced check
Wants my number, wants my time
Can't commit to a dinner at nine

[Pre-Chorus: harmonies stack, bass slides up]
And I've been patient, I've been kind
But I can't love a loading sign

[Chorus: three-part harmony, full beat]
You're buffering, buffering
I'm not gonna wait on a wheel that spins
Buffering, buffering
Hanging on a "soon" that never begins
I don't need a maybe on my line
Load it up or lose my time
You're buffering

[Rap Verse: third voice, quick and playful]
See, if you can't hold a date, can't hold a thought
Can't hold a door, then hold on, you're caught
I got bandwidth for joy, got bandwidth for peace
None for a man on a thirty-day lease
I'm not asking for the moon or the keys to a jet
Just a yes that's a yes and a text I can get

[Bridge: beat thins, lead alone, honest]
And if I'm fair, I've done it too
Kept somebody waiting on a "soon"
So this one's for the both of us
Show up, or give it up

[Final Chorus: three-part harmony, ad-libs, guitar riff on top]
You're buffering, buffering
I'm not gonna wait on a wheel that spins
Buffering, buffering
Hanging on a "soon" that never begins
I don't need a maybe on my line
Load it up or lose my time

[Outro: guitar riff alone, snaps, whispered]
Still loading
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 93 BPM, 4/4, G-sharp minor. Sleek, unhurried, clipped. Head-nod R&B with a raised eyebrow.

VOICE: Three women. A cool, low alto leads verse 1 with almost no vibrato. A lighter soprano takes verse 2. A third voice raps the middle section quickly and playfully. Choruses are close three-part harmony, soft and precise, with whispered ad-libs.

INSTRUMENTS: A picked nylon-string guitar riff that repeats throughout. A harpsichord-like synth doubling it an octave up. Deep, sliding synth bass. Crisp drum programming with rapid hi-hat stutters and a tight snare. Finger snaps. Subtle scratch effects. A soft string pad in the bridge.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar riff, harpsichord synth and snaps. 0:11 Verse 1. 0:32 Pre-chorus. 0:42 Chorus 1. 1:08 Verse 2. 1:29 Pre-chorus. 1:39 Chorus 2. 2:05 Rap verse, six lines. 2:21 Bridge, the beat thins and the lead admits her own part. 2:42 Final chorus with ad-libs and the guitar riff lifted in the mix. 3:13 Outro, riff and snaps, a whispered last line at 3:30.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-90s Atlanta R&B: glossy, spacious and precise, heavy low end, bright stuttering hi-hats, vocals soft but right at the front.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The opening line, delivered like a dictionary definition over the bare guitar riff.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The slang is from the streaming age, and the bridge does what the original did not: the singer includes herself. It is a standard to hold, not only a put-down.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Cool dismissal, wit, then a fair-minded admission.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

A new word for an old type: the person who is always almost there. The last verse admits the singer has been one too.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: dating in any decade; a friend who never commits to plans; an employer who keeps saying 'soon'; or a note to yourself about the life you keep postponing.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: a slang term defined in line one, a cool delivery, a picked guitar riff with a harpsichord-like synth, and a rap verse. Designed mishearing: 'buffering' is heard as 'suffering', which fits every chorus line.
